findings.body: The refactor claims sub-engine RNG isolation, but the orchestrator still runs every stage off the single shared `consts.rng` stream. Repo-wide search shows `deriveSubSeed` is never called outside its own unit test, so Stage 1/4a/3/4b remain coupled by call order exactly as before. That means the new decomposition did not actually buy the advertised protection against future PRNG drift: any later edit that adds/removes one `rng()` in an earlier stage will still silently perturb all downstream stages and can break byte-identical output without any local signal.
findings.recommendation: Either wire per-stage/per-visit RNGs from `deriveSubSeed(mainSeed, kind, visitIndex)` into the stage APIs now, or drop the B1.3 isolation claim and treat this as an incomplete refactor rather than shipped hardening.
findings.title: B1.3 sub-seed isolation was added but never integrated into the pipeline

findings.body: The new fuzz suite does not cover two of the failure modes it is supposed to guard. `P3` only checks that `romTrend` stays inside `{improved, slightly improved, stable}`, which still passes illegal floor regressions like `improved -> stable -> improved`. `P5` only enforces `current ⊆ previous`, so an engine that drops every associated symptom immediately still passes. For a stage-extraction refactor whose main risk is skipped state mutation or shifted RNG-driven transitions, these properties leave large blind spots and overstate confidence.
findings.recommendation: Strengthen the properties to assert actual longitudinal invariants: track prior ROM floors across visits, require symptom preservation from visit 1 unless a real rule permits shrinkage, and add a parity property that compares staged output against a known-good implementation or serialized visit-state invariants instead of only domain membership/subset checks.
findings.title: Property tests miss the exact regression classes introduced by the stage split

next_steps: Integrate `deriveSubSeed` into stage RNG construction or remove the unfulfilled isolation claim from the plan/acceptance criteria.
Replace P3/P5 with invariants that fail on skipped state writes and PRNG-order drift, then rerun the parity/snapshot suite.
result.summary: No current byte-drift was disproven, but the change still should not ship as-is: one advertised hardening step is not actually wired in, and the new fuzz evidence is too weak to catch the subtle refactor failures this branch is most exposed to.
